correctness.rationale: Encode each word by the weakly decreasing list of counts of b to the right of each successive a. Its area is K, and all lists in the A-by-B rectangle occur exactly once. The pattern abab occurs exactly when there are two distinct positive entries, so avoidance corresponds to a single rectangular block of positive entries and gives the divisor count, with the empty list of positive entries at K=0. For A>=2, aabb occurs exactly when the second entry is at least 2; otherwise a positive first entry t has r further ones followed by zeros, giving K=t+r, including the r=0 case and the all-zero case. This enumeration also works for A=1. For abba, avoidance is exactly that the largest and smallest entries differ by at most one; quotient and remainder of K by A specify the unique such list. Reversal and letter exchange yield all remaining cases. The zero-letter cases have a unique word and the partition-area generating function gives the Gaussian denominator. Explicit independent enumeration using all position quadruples agreed in 6552 cells for A+B<=12; this corroborates rather than replaces the general proof.
residual_risks: Scope is scattered patterns in finite linear binary words with two letters of each type in the forbidden pattern; no inference about arbitrary patterns.
